title: Investigate tr_b_01 mystery character
description:
tr_b_01 has full sprite archives (tr_b_01c.aar, tr_b_01_4c/5c/6c.aar) and chr_b entry with statC=57, but Tar-chan (Jungle King Tar-chan) supposedly has 0 battle characters in the game.

Questions to answer:
- What character is tr_b_01?
- Is it cut content, misattributed, or from a different series?
- Check if tr_b_01 sprites reveal the character identity
- Check koma.bin or text files for tr-related entries

comments.author: DJ
comments.text: RESOLVED: tr_b_01 is Taizo from 'Taizo Mote King Saga' - an UNUSED/CUT battle character. Evidence: 1) Full sprite archives exist (tr_b_01c.aar, tr_b_01_4c/5c/6c.aar), 2) Complete AI, collision, effect, shot data in chr/*, 3) Official game has 0 battle chars from this series, 4) TCRF mentions 'Momote Taizou' as unused, 5) chr_b entry exists at index 54 with formType=2, statC=57 (slow walk speed). Character was likely cut late in development.

comments.author: DJ
comments.text: CORRECTION: tr_b_01 is Tsuna Sawada & Reborn from 'Katekyo Hitman Reborn' - a legitimate battle character with 35 collision entries. The 'tr' prefix comes from 'kaTekyo hitman Reborn'. Taizo (the actual unused character from Taizo Mote King Saga) is dt_b_04 under the Meta/Debug category with only 1 collision entry and 'can only move, no attacks' per Character-Mapping.md. Original identification was incorrect.

title: Create reusable fighting game engine from discovered mechanics
description:
Long-term driving goal: Build a reusable, extensible 2D fighting game engine based on the mechanics reverse-engineered from Jump Ultimate Stars.

## Vision

Take the discovered game systems (damage formulas, knockback, passives, koma deck building, nature types, etc.) and implement them in a clean, documented, moddable engine that can be used for:
- Fan games
- Original fighting games with similar mechanics
- Educational purposes (understanding fighting game design)

## Key Systems to Implement

### Combat Core
- [ ] Damage calculation (jpower system, tier modifiers, nature advantage)
- [ ] Hitstun and combo system
- [ ] Knockback/displacement physics
- [ ] Guard and guard break mechanics

### Character System
- [ ] Character stats (walk speed tiers, weight classes)
- [ ] Passive abilities (per-form)
- [ ] Form variants (base/powered/special)
- [ ] Collision/hitbox system

### Deck/Team System
- [ ] Koma panel system (Help/Support/Battle)
- [ ] Ally boost mechanics
- [ ] Support character activation
- [ ] SP gauge and special moves

### Data-Driven Design
- [ ] JSON/YAML character definitions
- [ ] Moddable damage formulas
- [ ] Hot-reloadable data files
- [ ] Sprite animation system

## Dependencies

This epic depends on completing the reverse engineering research:
- Core Mechanics Research (JUS-9lp)
- File Format Documentation (JUS-0co)

## Success Criteria

1. Engine can load character data from config files
2. Two characters can fight with accurate JUS-like mechanics
3. Documentation sufficient for others to create characters
4. Code is clean, tested, and open source

title: Determine exact walk speed thresholds/tiers
description:
Walk speed is NOT linear with statC. Testing revealed at least 3 tiers:
- Zoro (statC=33) = SLOWEST
- Luffy (statC=82) = MIDDLE
- Ichigo (statC=225) = FASTEST
- Lenalee (statC=153) and Killua (statC=300) have SAME speed

Need to determine:
- Exact threshold values between tiers
- How many discrete speed tiers exist
- Whether it's threshold-based or lookup table
- Test more characters at boundary values (e.g., statC 70-100 range)

title: Investigate character passives system
description:
Some characters have passive abilities that affect gameplay mechanics:
- Edajima has 'hard to knock back' passive
- These passives modify knockback/displacement independent of base stats

Questions to answer:
- Where are passives stored? (chr_b.bin flags? separate file?)
- How do passives interact with displacement formula?
- What other passives exist in the game?
- How are passives displayed/triggered?

comments.author: DJ
comments.text:
PROGRESS: koma.bin analysis reveals structure:
- unk6 field = koma type (0=help, 1=support, 2=battle)
- unk7 field = likely passive/ability index
  - Battle komas: values 1-52 (small range)
  - Support komas: values 92-178 (larger range)
  
The unk7 value for battle komas is probably an index into a passive ability table in ARM9 or another file. Need to:
1. Find the passive ability table (search ARM9 for 52-entry or 192-entry tables)
2. Map unk7 values to known passives (Edajima's 'Principal', 3-step jump, etc.)
3. Verify by comparing Edajima's koma entry with known passive effects

comments.author: DJ
comments.text:
FINDINGS SUMMARY:

1. **Passive Storage Location:** koma.bin 'unk7' field (byte offset 6-7)
   - Each koma entry has a passive index
   - Battle komas (unk6=2): 47 unique passive indices (values 0-55)
   - Support komas (unk6=1): Different range (92-192)

2. **Known Passive Types (from web research):**
   - Knockback resistance (Edajima's 'Principal')
   - SP gain boost on KO (Edajima)
   - 3-step jump
   - Iron wall
   - Status abnormality resistance
   - Slash/Impact defense
   - Auto guard

3. **Next Steps:**
